question: Which memory-wiki isolation contract should OpenClaw support for shared-gateway multi-agent setups: plugin-owned per-agent/context-aware vault routing, generic agents.list[].plugins overrides, or explicitly unsupported shared-gateway isolation?
rationale: The source evidence proves the current global vault path, but the correct fix changes plugin config/API surface, security boundaries, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Design plugin-owned vault isolation
options.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned context-aware vault contract that covers agent/session precedence and no-context behavior without introducing a generic plugin override surface yet.

options.title: Wait for generic plugin overrides
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on a broader agents.list[].plugins design so all plugin config overrides share one core contract.

options.title: Document shared-gateway isolation as unsupported
options.body: Close the product gap by explicitly saying memory-wiki vaults are gateway-global unless users run separate gateways or configs.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned vault isolation
recommendation.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned context-aware vault contract that covers agent/session precedence and no-context behavior without introducing a generic plugin override surface yet.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin-config/runtime and memory-wiki storage history makes this the best available owner for the product/API boundary decision.
